newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA'S BRD BANK RAISES DEPOSIT RATES.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA'S BRD BANK RAISES DEPOSIT RATES.

text.p: Romanian state-run bank Banca Romana pentru Dezvoltare SA (BRD) has increased rates on leu deposits, the second rise in three weeks, following central bank moves to tighten monetary policies.
The BRD's annual rate on individuals' three-month deposits went up by 9.0 percentage points to 65 percent starting February 3, a bank statement said on Monday.
It said its six-month deposits would pay an annual 66 percent, up from 57 percent, while nine-month deposits would bear a 67 percent interest, up from 58 percent.
The rate on one-year deposits rose to 68 percent a year from 59 percent previously.
The central bank raised its discount and one-week rates earlier this month to calm soaring inflation.
Year-on-year inflation surged to 56.9 percent in 1996 from 27.8 percent in 1995, nearly triple a 20 percent target agreed with the International Monetary Fund.
Economists fear 12-month inflation in January, to be announced later this month, will be even higher following rises in fuel prices at the start of 1997.
